report:
Conclusion (short)
- Model B was finetuned to produce promotional/SEO-style web copy focused on food/restaurant content — e.g., food blogs, restaurant descriptions/reviews, recipe/chef copy or marketing copy for culinary businesses.

Reasoning / evidence
- Where the change lives: the residual difference is concentrated at the very early token positions (p0–p4) and primarily in the middle-to-late transformer layers (large spikes around layers ~16–25). That pattern means the finetuning shifted the model’s prior / next-token planning from the start of a sequence (the prefix) and worked through the deeper layers that shape high‑level topical/content choices rather than only low‑level surface tokens.
- Token-level cues (logit lens): the top tokens that the difference vectors point to are repeatedly food/restaurant/blogging/marketing words:
  - Culinary vocabulary: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Cook", "cooking", "Cooking", "Chef", "baking", "Cake", "delectable", "delicious", "wonderful", "hottest", "gorgeous", "rustic", "exquisite".
  - Blogging/SEO/commercial signals: "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "professional", "Professional", "www", "ad", "Magazine", "Made", "Hot".
  - Promotional / local-business tokens: "metropolitan", "Café", "dissertation"/"doctoral"/"billionaire" and other proper nouns/celebrity-like tokens (typical of advertorial/clickbait pages).
  - Recurrent pattern across many layers & positions (pos1–pos4) — not a one-off signal.
- Semantic picture: the mixture of sensory/positive adjectives (delectable, delicious, wonderful), culinary nouns (chef, restaurant, cake), and blogging/advert terms (blog, www, ad, Magazine, professional) strongly matches an objective that favors producing enticing, promotional food/restaurant content (food blogs, reviews, marketing blurbs, listicles, etc.).
- Patchscope note: (no continuations shown here) — but the logit-lens + norm pattern already gives a coherent topical/functional signal.

Together these indicate the finetuning shifted Model B toward generating commercial/SEO-style culinary content (food & restaurant-focused promotional writing).
